$comment: Reference test PDFs vendored from upstream projects, with provenance.
Every file is pinned to the upstream commit it was taken from and carries a
SHA-256, so `pwsh testdata/fetch.ps1` can prove the committed bytes are the
bytes upstream published rather than something that drifted or was rewritten.
Selection rule: a file is here only if upstream authored it AS a reference
fixture. Bug-report attachments (pymupdf's test_NNNN.pdf, named for the issue
that produced them) are excluded — upstream cannot grant rights to a file a
third party uploaded to a tracker. Copies of the ISO 32000 specifications are
excluded for the same reason the sponsored PDFs in docs/ are gitignored: they
are ISO's copyright regardless of which repo redistributes them.
See docs/test.docs.md for what each file is for and why it was chosen.

sources.license_note: Generated for this repo from the .tex sources committed beside each PDF, so these are ours to redistribute — unlike the sponsored ISO documents in docs/, which are the corpus we measure against but cannot ship. This is why the fidelity tests run in every clone and the corpus tests skip.
$comment: The yardstick: six single-concern PDFs, each beside a hand-written .gold.md
of what it should convert to. The gold files are written from the .tex
source's intent and never from a reader's output — deriving them from an
Acrobat export would only prove we agree with Acrobat, which is the opposite
of an independent reference. See testdata/reference/README.md.
No upstream 'commit' or fetch entry: fetch.ps1 verifies vendored bytes match
what upstream published, and these have no upstream. The SHA-256s below still
pin them, so a fixture that changes without its gold file changing is visible.

files.why: Heading sequence at three depths, untagged: the layout path infers level from size and weight
Bold, italic, bold-italic and monospace mid-sentence — a run that bleeds past its words is a font-trait misread
Bulleted items with one nested level; the markers arrive as text because the layout path has no list role
Ruled 3x3 table: every cell's text must survive, which column gaps threaten by splitting or joining cells
One image and one caption: 'no prose' must be distinguishable from lost prose, which is what the empty-output warning and the OCR router both depend on

The only tagged fixture, and the path every corpus document takes: five numbered clauses at three depths, each with its body, joined on (page, MCID). Built with lualatex because pdfTeX's tagging backend writes the same /MCID into every /MCR, which silently drops every body paragraph
The image inside image.pdf: three flat colour bands at 64x48, flat so extracted pixels are checkable and non-square so a transposed read shows in the dimensions

sources.license_note: Data fixtures, aggregated not linked: vendoring them does not affect this repo's MIT licensing of its own code. Kept in their own directory with attribution so the boundary is visible.

files.why: Symbol font glyph set — the encoding case with no Unicode round-trip
Type3 font: glyphs are content streams, widths in glyph space
Defective font dictionaries — must lose glyphs, not the page
Ligatures: one glyph to many characters, the 'ecient' failure
Line-break joining and inter-word spacing
Minimal table, ruled — layout-path table detection
Tagged table with styling — the tagged-path counterpart
Dashed rules: table borders that are not solid strokes
CJK in tables: CID fonts, no inter-word spaces to infer
Baseline opaque image
Transparent image — an /SMask from a producer other than the ISO corpus
Page with neither fonts nor images: the empty-of-everything routing case
Several image codecs in one file
Cyclic outline tree — termination, not a hang
285-page technical manual, Type1 + Type3, real code samples. The negative control for monospace detection
arXiv paper: LaTeX-produced Type1, two-column
Mixed TrueType/Type0/Type1 in one document

sources.license_note: Same as above. The OCR directory is the reason this repo is here: it ships a scanned page, the same page OCRed, and the expected text as a .txt — a genuine ground truth.

files.why: Smallest useful text document — a fast smoke fixture
Scanned page, no text layer at all: the OCR path's input
The same page after Tesseract: invisible text layer in GlyphLessFont
GROUND TRUTH for ocr-ed.pdf. The only file here that states what the right answer is
A second OCR engine's text layer, so the fix is not tuned to Tesseract

sources.license_note: Adobe's own sample inputs, MIT, same licence as this repo. The two ISO 32000 PDFs in AdobeDocs/pdfservices-api-documentation were deliberately NOT taken: Apache-2.0 on the repo does not make ISO's specification Apache-2.0.

files.why: Adobe's auto-tag sample: untagged input for the accessibility pipeline
Adobe's Extract sample — properly tagged, the reference for a StructTreeRoot that works
Multi-page with 14 images, TrueType + Type0
Adobe's OCR input: 4 scanned pages, no fonts
A StructTreeRoot holding only two Document elements — the producer-stub case probe.go's heuristic exists for
Tagged single page with a figure — small enough to reason about by hand
Zero bytes. Upstream ships it deliberately as an invalid input: must fail with a reason, not panic
151 pages, zero fonts, zero images — Adobe's own disqualified-input fixture

sources.license_note: Not PDFs. These are DocTags documents and the Markdown docling itself renders them to — the ground-truth pairs for ocr/doctags. MIT, the same licence as this repo. They matter because they make the parser testable with no model running and no GPU: DocTags is granite-docling's output format, and these are the format's own author's expectations.

files.why: The wide case: 9 pages of a real paper, every tag the parser must handle — 5 OTSL tables with lcel/ucel spans, 6 pictures with nested captions, 8 page_breaks, unordered lists, footnotes
docling's own Markdown for the file above: the ground truth this repo's Markdown sink is measured against, so a disagreement is visible rather than argued
The smallest complete document, and the only fixture with a <chart> holding a picture-classification token (<bar_chart>) before its OTSL grid
Ground truth for barchart.dt, small enough to read whole
One page as the model actually emits it — a scanned page's worth of OTSL, page_header and page_footer, unwrapped by any document assembly step
Upstream's deliberately-degenerate case: tags with no <loc_> coordinates at all. A model that stops emitting locations must still parse, which is the no-panics gate applied to model output
Ground truth for the degenerate case, and the pin for a surprise: docling renders section_header_level_1 as `###`, not `##`
